subject: design-technology
title: Marking & Measuring
welcome_lead: Steel rule, try square, pencil — getting the layout right.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: marking tools, measuring, accuracy.

walkthroughs.body_html: Use a steel rule for straight lines, a try square for right angles, and a pencil on wood or a scriber on metal. Marks should be clear but not gouged.
If two parts aren't square (at 90 degrees), nothing will fit. Always check with the try square before cutting — sliding it along an edge to test the angle.
Tolerance is how much error is allowed. A tolerance of +/- 0.5 mm means anything within half a mm is fine. Tighter tolerances cost more to make.
